issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: The appraisal of permanent physical bodily damage is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile, which centers on anger, distrust, hypervigilance, and media avoidance after police violence but contains no corroborating threat or memory content about ongoing somatic injury, pain, disability, or bodily fragility. It stands out as a different trauma consequence than the remainder of the formulation.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Gambling: I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
issues.explanation: Gambling used for excitement/distracting is weakly connected to the rest of the selected profile. The dominant formulation is Threat ↔ Negative Appraisals with trauma-memory-linked fear/anger and avoidance of feelings/media. Gambling for excitement does not clearly address the specific threat, memory, or appraisal pattern represented elsewhere, making it the least coherent maladaptive strategy in this set.

vignette: Ahmad is a 56-year-old Middle Eastern man who works as a Social Media Manager. He has been married for over three decades and is deeply affected by an encounter with police violence that occurred six months ago. This traumatic event left him struggling to reconcile his sense of self, leading to significant psychological distress. The night of the incident, Ahmad was walking home from work when he witnessed a young man being aggressively detained by officers. As the situation escalated, one officer turned toward Ahmad and demanded identification. In the ensuing confrontation, the officer shoved Ahmad to the ground, causing him to fall violently against a curb and hit his head. The officer’s actions were accompanied by harsh, threatening language that filled Ahmad with an overwhelming sense of fear and rage. Since this event, Ahmad has been tormented by fragmented memories of the incident, often triggered by similar sights or sounds in his daily life. He reports vividly tasting the metallic tang of blood from the fall whenever he recalls the moment. The intensity of these memories is compounded by a strong urge to block them out before they can fully resurface, leaving him with only glimpses of the trauma. Ahmad’s sense of trust has been profoundly shaken. He now believes that people are not what they seem and that the world is inherently dangerous. This pervasive distrust fuels his maladaptive strategies, leading him to avoid any situation or stimulus that might elicit strong emotions, whether positive or negative. As a result, he no longer watches TV programs or reads news articles that could remind him of similar events. His inability to relax even in safe environments is another manifestation of the ongoing threat he feels. Ahmad constantly scans his surroundings for signs of potential danger and always identifies escape routes before feeling comfortable anywhere. This heightened state of alertness has made it difficult for him to engage fully with his work as a Social Media Manager, where he often finds himself distracted by these safety concerns. The intense negative emotions associated with the memory of the incident—fear, anger, and guilt—have only reinforced Ahmad’s belief that the world is dangerous. This cycle perpetuates itself: his sense of danger fuels his avoidance behaviors and heightened threat monitoring, which in turn intensify his distrust of others and his negative self-appraisals. Ahmad has come to believe that he violated his own values during the incident, adding another layer of distress. The memory triggers intense rage, further deepening his mistrust and aversion to situations where he might feel vulnerable or exposed. Over time, Ahmad’s maladaptive strategies have begun to isolate him from friends and family, as he avoids social gatherings and even some professional events that might trigger these memories. His wife has noticed a significant change in his behavior but finds it difficult to understand the depth of his distress. What finally brought Ahmad to seek help was a realization that his avoidance behaviors were becoming increasingly disruptive to both his work and personal life. He is most afraid of losing control over his emotions and feeling trapped by these memories, yet he also hopes for a sense of peace and a way to reclaim his trust in others and the world around him. Ahmad’s journey toward recovery will require addressing the complex interplay between his negative appraisals, maladaptive strategies, memory fragments, and ongoing perceptions of threat. Through therapy, he aims to find a path toward healing that allows him to reengage with life without the constant shadow of fear and suspicion.
